source.name: Arrow keys in a tab list must move keyboard focus to the newly selected tab
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/37200) at 0a5f6e078c9cb9ecca9ab90b3984c5f792a11bae. Blind to the maintainers' fix d49d8ce583f6f12552f122122a99063738656cd9; routing auto.

journey.title: Walk the settings tabs with arrow keys
journey.goal: Each arrow press selects and focuses the next tab

functionalJourney.title: Switch settings sections with the mouse
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a tab shows its panel

guards.title: Tab from the active tab into its panel
guards.goal: Tab leaves the tab list for the active panel

plan.root_cause: The tab widget's arrow key navigation does not move focus to the newly selected tab; it only updates ARIA state and leaves focus on the previously blurred tab or the body, causing a mismatch between visual selection and keyboard focus.
plan.repair_strategy: Add an explicit focus() call to the next tab element before activating it in the _keydown handler, ensuring focus follows selection as required by the ARIA tablist pattern.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft keystrokes will move focus to the adjacent tab, update its aria-selected state, and display the corresponding panel, making the tablist operable via keyboard as required by WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: If the next tab is disabled, focus will not move (existing behavior).
Calling focus() before show() could theoretically cause two focus events, but show() does not change focus, so risk is minimal.
Ensure that the focus method does not interfere with any custom handlers attached to the tab elements.
verification_requirements: After focusing the first tab, pressing ArrowRight results in focus on the second tab and its aria-selected becoming true.
Pressing ArrowRight again moves focus to the third tab with appropriate state updates.
Tab panels update visibility in sync with the selected tab.
No unintended scrolling or page changes occur due to focus movement.
